title: commitwork manifest
description: Maps a repo's GitHub Actions workflows to local-equivalent commands so CI can be run on a developer machine without spending GitHub Actions minutes.

repo.description: Human label for the repo this manifest drives.

repoPath.description: Absolute path to the target repo. If omitted, the runner uses --repo, $COMMITWORK_REPO, or the current working directory.

images.description: Container images the sweep pulls ONCE before the first repo (monitor/images.mjs), bounded, recording presence + digest in batch-manifest.json. Lanes never `--pull=always` per repo: that cost a registry round-trip per repo and hung a sweep 8.9 h on one stalled pull.

groups.description: Named ordered lists of check ids, e.g. quick / standard / all. `commitwork run <group>` runs the listed checks in order.

id.description: Stable check id, conventionally matching the workflow filename stem.

remediationPrompt.description: A prompt an operator can feed to an AI coding assistant to remediate this scanner's findings — templated guidance, not per-finding text.

formatNotes.description: Scanner-specific FORMAT FACTS composed into every triage handoff alongside remediationPrompt — the exact mechanics of this scanner's suppression/config syntax (e.g. a .gitleaksignore line IS the finding's Fingerprint field, verbatim). Exists because models invent plausible-but-wrong syntax when the mechanics are not supplied.

workflow.description: Path (relative to repoPath) to the GitHub workflow this check mirrors. Used by --act.

timeoutSec.description: Wall-clock bound in seconds for this check. The runner kills the command group AND removes the containers it named (cw-<slice>-<repo>-<check>*), records status noscan with the reason, sets the report aside as <file>.killed and writes <file>.exit=124. Omitted ⇒ CW_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SEC, else 1800 — above every lane's measured maximum on the 100-repo corpus except the two that declare their own.

local.description: Shell commands run in sequence (fail-fast) in repoPath. This is the local equivalent of the workflow's actual checks.

act.description: Faithful execution via nektos/act. Present only for checks where running the real YAML adds value (e.g. SARIF-producing scans).

job.description: Optional specific job id to run (act -j).

requires.description: Gating conditions. A check whose requirements are unmet is skipped (or fails under --strict).

tools.description: Executables that must be on PATH.

secrets.description: Env vars that must be set (checked in process env and repoPath/.env).

services.description: Free-text service prerequisites surfaced to the user (e.g. 'docker daemon', 'live Supabase'). Informational.

report.description: Declares the structured artifact this check writes (into $CW_REPORT_DIR) so `scan` can parse finding counts.

log.description: Filename (under $CW_REPORT_DIR) of the tool's own log. Declared so coverageSignals has something to read: a tool that loses a capability usually announces it on stderr and still exits 0, so the exit sidecar alone cannot detect it. A declared log that is absent or unreadable makes coverage 'unknown', never 'full'.

format.description: Report format. THIS LIST IS THE CODE'S, not a hand-kept copy: it is PARSED_FORMATS union PASSTHROUGH_FORMATS from bin/commitwork.mjs, and bin/test/manifest-schema-drift.test.mjs fails if the two diverge. It had drifted 11 formats behind (a11y, actionlint, authz-bola, cspm-github, depscan, gradle-wrapper, minify, schemathesis, scorecard, shellcheck, tls-headers) because nothing validated any manifest against this schema — the drift was invisible, not tolerated.

executesRepoCode.description: This lane runs the scanned repository's own build, test or install code. Unsandboxed, its row carries isolation 'none' and coverage 'reduced'.

requiresRepoTrust.description: The lane's command runs a script the scanned repository supplies, not a bundled scanner. It executes only when the run was given --trust-repo-manifest (or COMMITWORK_TRUST_REPO_MANIFEST=1); otherwise the lane reports noscan with the reason 'repo-supplied script; pass --trust-repo-manifest to run it', never a pass and never a finding.

egress.description: What this lane reaches over the network, declared so the host sandbox can deny everything else. THIS LIST IS THE CODE'S: EGRESS_CLASSES in bin/lib/sandbox.mjs, and bin/test/manifest-egress.test.mjs fails if the two diverge. `none` runs with the network denied (isolation 'full'); every other class runs with the filesystem confined and the network open (isolation 'fs-only'). A check without this key is never wrapped with a guessed class: it runs unsandboxed with the reason recorded on its row, and bin/test/manifest-egress.test.mjs fails on any bundled check that omits it.

sandboxExtraReads.description: Paths this lane must read beyond the host sandbox's fixed set (the scanned tree, commitwork, the system prefixes, the node prefix, TMPDIR, the prefix of each `requires.tools` binary, ~/.gitconfig). `~/` is the operator home, `./` is the scanned tree, anything else is absolute. Declared per lane so a credential read (posture-scorecard's ~/.config/gh) is visible where the lane is, not buried in a profile.

sandboxExtraWrites.description: Paths this lane must write beyond $CW_REPORT_DIR and TMPDIR: a tool's own cache (~/.semgrep, ~/Library/Caches/trivy, ~/.codeql). A write path is readable too, because a cache is read back. Same prefixes as sandboxExtraReads. Per lane on purpose: a lane that executes repository code and also writes a cache another lane later executes from is a supply-chain path, and the declaration is what makes it reviewable.

coverageSignals.description: Patterns in this check's log that mean a LANE OF THE CHECK DID NOT RUN, even though the tool exited 0. Coverage is orthogonal to severity: a check can find real findings while half-blind, and these two facts must never be reported as one number. Declared per check rather than guessed centrally because only the check's author knows which of its chatter means a capability died. A pattern that matches sets coverage 'reduced' and names the lane; a pattern that fails to compile sets 'unknown', never 'full'.

pattern.description: JavaScript regular expression source, tested against the declared report.log.

lane.description: The capability that was lost, in a reader's words — this is what gets reported, not the regex. e.g. 'Go call analysis'.

denominatorPattern.description: Optional. A regex counting the units the tool DID process, so the reason can state k of n instead of a bare 'reduced'. Without it the gap's SIZE is unknown and the reason says so. Only claimed when the denominator matches at least once: 'k of 0' is a broken declaration, not a coverage statement.

capture.description: Capture group index in `pattern` naming the unit that failed (default 1). Those names are listed in the reason, capped at 8.

unit.description: What is being counted, singular, for the reason text. e.g. 'yarn.lock'. Defaults to 'file'.

appliesIfExists.description: During `scan`, only run this check if at least one of these paths exists in the repo (e.g. package.json).

appliesIfGit.description: During `scan`, only run this check if the target is a git repo.

appliesIfSourceExt.description: Only run this check if a source file with one of these extensions exists in the tree (bounded walk, vendored/build dirs skipped). The signal is the sources themselves — use this instead of appliesIfExists when a build manifest is the wrong proxy (CodeQL's JS extractor needs .js/.ts sources, not a package.json).

requiresUrl.description: Runtime scanner: needs a live base URL (--url/--urls/commitwork.url/$CW_TARGET_URL). Without one the check records a visible coverage void, never a silent pass.

producesIfExists.description: Artifact globs (e.g. *.jar) that must exist somewhere in the repo for an empty-clean result to be trustworthy; otherwise the check is recorded as a void ('no scannable artifact — build first').

groups.description: Membership tags; lets `run <group>` select this check in addition to the top-level groups map.

skipsOnGitHub.description: Workflow steps deliberately NOT reproduced locally (SARIF upload, PR comments, artifact retention, cloud uploads). Documentation only.

scopeNotes.description: Named limits on what this check can see (e.g. 'language', 'codeql-extractor-baseline'). In use on 17 checks and unknown to this schema until 2026-08-25.

aliasOf.description: This check reports into another check's category. In use on 2 checks and unknown to this schema until 2026-08-25.

excludedFrom.description: Groups this check is deliberately held OUT of. Cross-checked against the real selector (bin/commitwork.mjs groupMembers, the union of the top-level groups map and each check's own groups tag) by bin/test/build-mode-containment.test.mjs, in both directions.

reason.description: Why the exclusion exists, in terms a reader can check. Length-floored on purpose: a containment without a substantive reason is a coverage gap wearing a label.

reviewBy.description: When this exclusion must be revisited, as an ISO-8601 UTC instant. Pinned with `pattern` and not `format`: monitor/registry.mjs implements type/enum/required/pattern/minLength/minItems/additionalProperties and NOT format, and it refuses a schema using an unimplemented keyword rather than passing everything against it — an unenforced constraint is worse than none, because it reads as enforced. A containment nobody returns to is class E2, a suppression outliving its judgement, applied to coverage.

containment.description: A lane's exclusion from a group, declared as DATA rather than argued in prose. It exists because sast-codeql-swift carried a formatNotes sentence claiming it sat in `deep` only while its groups were ["all","deep"]: the claim and the enforcement were two different objects and only one of them ran. Three sweeps under group "all" then executed third-party build tooling from repositories this fleet does not own.

groupsNote.description: Prose beside `groups`, carrying WHY a check is or is not in a group. Recognised because manifests/build-health.json and quality-gates.json have carried it since they were written, and additionalProperties:false was silently refusing both — nothing validated this file, so the disagreement was invisible. Matches the repo-wide *Note convention (areasNote, excludeNote, lifecycleNote in projects.json): rationale lives beside the thing it explains, not in a separate doc that rots apart from it.

ghaSafety.description: Prose stating why this manifest's checks are safe with respect to GitHub Actions invocation — typically that no project declares them, so a sweep or GHA `all` never reaches them. Recognised for the same reason as groupsNote: manifests/runtime.json has carried it, unread by any source and unvalidated by anything.
